FSQ01.name: Revenue Growth
FSQ01.forensic_rationale: Growth is neither inherently good nor bad; assess against cash flow, WC and sector context.

FSQ02.name: Receivables Growth vs Revenue Growth
FSQ02.forensic_rationale: Widening AR-vs-revenue growth can indicate weak collectability or aggressive revenue recognition.

FSQ03.name: DSRI
FSQ03.forensic_rationale: Beneish-derived deterioration in receivables relative to sales.

FSQ04.name: Revenue Quality Ratio (CFO/Revenue)
FSQ04.forensic_rationale: Tests whether reported revenue translates into operating cash.

FSQ05.name: Gross Margin Change
FSQ05.forensic_rationale: Large unexplained margin changes can reflect recognition or classification issues.

FSQ06.name: Operating Margin Change
FSQ06.forensic_rationale: Sharp unexplained operating-margin expansion warrants review.

FSQ07.name: Net Margin Change
FSQ07.forensic_rationale: Large unexplained net-margin changes may be driven by non-operating/accounting items.

FSQ08.name: Other Income / PAT
FSQ08.forensic_rationale: High non-core income contribution reduces confidence in core earnings.

FSQ09.name: Exceptional Items / PAT
FSQ09.forensic_rationale: Material exceptional items distort earnings quality and comparability.

FSQ10.name: Tax Rate Anomaly
FSQ10.forensic_rationale: Unusual tax rates can materially support reported earnings.

FSQ11.name: Earnings vs Revenue Divergence
FSQ11.forensic_rationale: Profit growth far above sales growth requires evidence of sustainability.

FSQ12.name: EPS vs PAT Divergence
FSQ12.forensic_rationale: Reconcile dilution, buybacks and other capital actions.

FSQ13.name: Revenue Concentration
FSQ13.forensic_rationale: High concentration increases the importance of validating revenue sustainability.

FSQ14.name: Contract Liabilities / Revenue
FSQ14.forensic_rationale: Contract liabilities can corroborate or challenge revenue timing.

FSQ15.name: Deferred Revenue Change
FSQ15.forensic_rationale: Unusual deferred-revenue movements require billing/cash reconciliation.

CFI02.name: CFO / EBITDA
CFI02.forensic_rationale: Tests conversion of operating earnings into cash.

CFI03.name: CFO Margin
CFI03.forensic_rationale: Low operating cash relative to revenue reduces earnings confidence.

CFI04.name: Free Cash Flow
CFI04.forensic_rationale: Persistent weak FCF despite profits warrants investigation.

CFI06.name: CFO Growth vs PAT Growth
CFI06.forensic_rationale: Earnings growth without cash growth is a key warning.

CFI07.name: CFO Volatility
CFI07.forensic_rationale: High volatility can indicate inconsistent cash conversion.

CFI08.name: Cash Interest Coverage
CFI08.forensic_rationale: Weak cash coverage can increase reporting pressure.

CFI10.name: CFO Less CapEx / PAT
CFI10.forensic_rationale: Tests cash earnings after capital investment.

CFI11.name: Cash Conversion Trend
CFI11.forensic_rationale: Persistent deterioration is more informative than one-year noise.

CFI12.name: Working Capital Contribution to CFO
CFI12.forensic_rationale: CFO mainly generated by temporary WC movements is less sustainable.

CFI13.name: Non-cash Operating Items / CFO
CFI13.forensic_rationale: Large non-cash reconciliation items warrant review.

CFI15.name: Investing Cash Flow Anomaly
CFI15.forensic_rationale: Unusual investing flows can affect cash-quality interpretation.

AQ01.name: Total Accruals
AQ01.forensic_rationale: Measures accounting profit not supported by cash.

AQ02.name: Total Accruals / Average Assets
AQ02.forensic_rationale: Scales accrual intensity by asset base.

AQ03.name: Sloan Accrual Ratio
AQ03.forensic_rationale: Established accrual-quality signal; exact published specification and calibration must be frozen.

AQ04.name: Working Capital Accruals / Assets
AQ04.forensic_rationale: Detects earnings effects concentrated in working capital.

AQ06.name: Accrual Trend
AQ06.forensic_rationale: Persistent deterioration is more concerning than isolated accruals.

AQ07.name: Accrual Volatility
AQ07.forensic_rationale: High volatility may indicate unusual accounting adjustments.

AQ08.name: Change in Net Operating Assets
AQ08.forensic_rationale: Rapid NOA growth can accompany aggressive recognition/capitalization.

AQ09.name: Accruals vs Revenue Growth
AQ09.forensic_rationale: Accrual growth materially above business growth is a warning.

AQ10.name: Accruals vs CFO Divergence
AQ10.forensic_rationale: Identifies earnings expansion without cash support.

AQ11.name: Depreciation / CapEx
AQ11.forensic_rationale: Changes may indicate useful-life or capitalization issues.

AQ12.name: D&A / Gross PPE
AQ12.forensic_rationale: Unusual depreciation intensity warrants useful-life review.

AQ13.name: Deferred Tax Contribution to PAT
AQ13.forensic_rationale: Large deferred-tax effects can alter earnings without current cash.

AQ14.name: Provision / Expense Ratio
AQ14.forensic_rationale: Large estimate changes can affect expense timing.

AQ15.name: Reserve Reversal Contribution
AQ15.forensic_rationale: Material reversals can inflate current earnings.

WCH03.name: Receivables / Revenue
WCH03.forensic_rationale: Measures receivable intensity; sector calibration required.

WCH04.name: Inventory Days
WCH04.forensic_rationale: Detects inventory buildup; sector calibration required.

WCH05.name: Inventory Growth vs Revenue Growth
WCH05.forensic_rationale: Detects stock buildup ahead of sales.

WCH06.name: Inventory Turnover
WCH06.forensic_rationale: Low turnover can indicate slow-moving or overstated inventory.

WCH07.name: DPO
WCH07.forensic_rationale: Sharp increases may indicate liquidity pressure/supplier financing.

WCH08.name: Payables Growth vs COGS Growth
WCH08.forensic_rationale: Detects supplier balances growing faster than activity.

WCH10.name: Operating WC / Revenue
WCH10.forensic_rationale: Measures working-capital intensity; sector calibration required.

WCH11.name: Working Capital Growth vs Revenue Growth

WCH13.name: Inventory Provision Coverage
WCH13.forensic_rationale: Low provision coverage alongside aging inventory can be a valuation red flag.

WCH14.name: Contract Asset / Revenue
WCH14.forensic_rationale: High contract assets may indicate revenue recognized before billing rights.

WCH15.name: Supplier Financing Indicators
WCH15.forensic_rationale: Supplier financing can alter operating-cash interpretation.

BSI02.name: AQI
BSI02.forensic_rationale: Beneish Asset Quality Index; higher values indicate deterioration.

BSI03.name: Intangibles / Total Assets
BSI03.forensic_rationale: High intangible intensity increases valuation/impairment judgment.

BSI04.name: Goodwill / Total Assets
BSI04.forensic_rationale: High goodwill concentration increases impairment sensitivity.

BSI05.name: Capitalized Development Costs / Assets
BSI05.forensic_rationale: Material capitalization can defer expense recognition.

BSI06.name: Capitalized Software / Revenue
BSI06.forensic_rationale: Large capitalization relative to revenue may defer expenses.

BSI07.name: PPE Growth vs Revenue Growth
BSI07.forensic_rationale: Detects asset buildup ahead of business growth.

BSI08.name: CapEx / Depreciation
BSI08.forensic_rationale: Divergence can reflect expansion, under-depreciation or capitalization.

BSI10.name: Off-Balance-Sheet Exposure
BSI10.forensic_rationale: Material obligations can distort headline ratios.

BSI11.name: Contingent Liabilities / Equity
BSI11.forensic_rationale: Measures potential claims relative to capital.

BSI12.name: Lease Liabilities / Assets
BSI12.forensic_rationale: Captures material lease commitments; sector context required.

BSI14.name: Asset Impairment Reversals / PAT
BSI14.forensic_rationale: Detects earnings supported by impairment reversals.

BSI15.name: Asset-to-Revenue Divergence
BSI15.forensic_rationale: Asset growth materially ahead of revenue requires explanation.

GS01.name: Revenue CAGR
GS01.forensic_rationale: Growth must be corroborated by cash and working capital.

GS02.name: PAT CAGR
GS02.forensic_rationale: Earnings growth must be tested for recurrence and cash support.

GS03.name: EBITDA CAGR
GS03.forensic_rationale: Operating earnings growth is tested against revenue and cash.

GS06.name: Margin Sustainability
GS06.forensic_rationale: Tests whether growth relies on unusual margin changes.

GS09.name: Growth Funding Gap
GS09.forensic_rationale: Identifies growth requiring external funding despite reported profits.

GS10.name: Organic vs Acquired Growth
GS10.forensic_rationale: Separates underlying growth from acquisition-driven growth.

GD01.name: Qualified Audit Opinion
GD01.forensic_rationale: Formal auditor opinion is high-value external evidence.

GD02.name: Key Audit Matter Severity
GD02.forensic_rationale: KAMs identify areas of significant auditor judgment.

GD03.name: Auditor Change
GD03.forensic_rationale: Auditor changes require review of disclosed reasons.

GD06.name: Promoter / Insider Pledge
GD06.forensic_rationale: High pledging can indicate financing pressure.

GD07.name: Accounting Policy Change
GD07.forensic_rationale: Policy changes can affect earnings timing/comparability.

GD08.name: Restatement / Prior Period Adjustments
GD08.forensic_rationale: Restatements are direct evidence of prior reporting reliability issues.

GD09.name: Regulatory / Enforcement Action
GD09.forensic_rationale: External enforcement is strong corroborating evidence.

GD10.name: Litigation / Accounting Contingency Exposure
GD10.forensic_rationale: Reporting-related disputes can signal unresolved accounting risk.

MODEL01.name: Beneish M-Score
MODEL01.forensic_rationale: Foundational earnings-manipulation screening signal; show canonical -1.78 cutoff separately; never label it proof of fraud.

MODEL02.name: Sloan Accrual Model
MODEL02.forensic_rationale: Established accrual-quality signal; exact formula/bands must be frozen to selected source.

MODEL03.name: Altman Z-Score
MODEL03.forensic_rationale: Financial-distress context; not evidence of accounting fraud by itself.

MODEL04.name: Piotroski F-Score
MODEL04.forensic_rationale: Financial-strength context; not itself a fraud score.

MODEL05.name: Ohlson O-Score
MODEL05.forensic_rationale: Distress/default context; not itself evidence of manipulation.
